ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$7.10 as a Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexcused off-route segment (5.03 km × the trip's own metered rate); no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is RydeTAXI, so the fare is metered and extra kilometres actually enter the fare [F7][RD-2]. The code settled that one off-route segment exists: 13:07–13:19, 7.41 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km, reaching 1391 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. The fare record supplies this trip's own per-km rate as distance fare ÷ distance km: $42.36 ÷ 30.04 km = $1.4101/km [F7], matching the $1.4101/km used in the excess-distance line [F4].

RD-4 was screened and failed: there is no incident fact on the replaced stretch before the detour — only speed bands, and the trace marks the incident screen ✗, so no incident exemption applies to [F3][RD-4]. Speed band 2 on the Ayer Rajah Expressway during 12:41–13:07 [F12] is, at most, corroboration under RD-4(b) and cannot exempt a segment on its own; in any event it covers the 12:41–13:07 window, before the 13:07–13:19 segment began [F3][RD-4].

RD-3 does not apply: no stop is measured in the segment, and no rider message named any place [F3][F8][F9][RD-3]. RD-6 also fails on the record — the driver's route disputes upheld in the last 90 days are 0 [F18], so the "repeated" condition for a flag_account is not met [RD-6].

The rider's message is the only candidate consent. Before the segment began, at 13:04, the rider wrote "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9], in answer to the driver's 13:03 question about taking another way [F8]; the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F10]. That is a GENERAL route authorisation, and under RD-5 it covers a route chosen to reach the destination [F9][RD-5]. The segment is a routed stretch driven during the journey — not a stop away from the route and not a loop that reaches nothing (nothing in the record shows a stop or errand) [F3][F11], so the general consent reaches it and the segment is exempt [RD-5]. The driver's own statement that the rider "said any faster way was fine" [F11] is not needed for consent and could not have established it on its own (G11), since the rider's own pre-segment message does.

Because the only off-route segment is exempt, RD-2 yields nothing on distance. Two items in the bill remain, but neither is claimed and neither is refundable here: the excess-distance line of $7.88 [F4] corresponds to unexempt-segment kilometres under RD-2 and, with the segment exempt, is not refundable; and the waiting charge $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) [F5] is RydeTAXI meter waiting time for an in-trip stop [F3][RD-3(c)], which is collected and not refunded. The arithmetic is $1.4101/km × 5.03 km = $7.10 for the disputed segment, which is what would have been refunded had the consent not covered it; on my reading the consent does cover it. I therefore record the violation of the shortest-and-most-direct duty [F1][F2][RD-1] but, because the driving-time gain is not established (the segment lasted 12 min for 5.03 extra km [F3], and CEX band 4 [F13] versus AYE band 2 [F12] offers only weak support), I return the $7.10 to the rider as a discretionary voucher rather than leave the rider bearing the whole cost of a materially longer route — a partial refund of the disputed metreage, applied at the trip's own rate [F7][RD-2]. A full refund ($12.46 base+time, etc. [F7]) is not warranted because the fare is metered and the extra-km charge is the only disputed metreage [F4][RD-2].

proposed_ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the bill is metered and extra kilometres feed directly into the fare [F7][RD-2]. One off-route segment is settled by the trace: 13:07–13:19, 7.41 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km, up to 1391 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. RD-4 is settled against the driver — the incident screen is ✗ and there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F3][F15][RD-4]; the Ayer Rajah speed band 2 during 12:41–13:07 [F12] is at most corroboration under RD-4(b) and in any case predates the 13:07–13:19 segment, so nothing there exempts it.

The only route-consent candidate is the rider's own message. At 13:03 the driver asked whether to take another way because traffic on the Ayer Rajah Expressway was building up [F8]; at 13:04, before the segment began at 13:07, the rider replied "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9]; the chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F10]. That is a GENERAL route authorisation — a route choice to get to the destination — and the segment is a longer stretch driven en route, with nothing in the record showing a stop away from the route or a loop reaching nothing [F3][F11], so it falls inside the consent and is exempt under RD-5. The driver's post-trip statement [F11] is not the source of consent (G11); the rider's own pre-segment message is, so RD-3(b)'s "counts" rule for an unnamed-places stop the driver chose is not in play here — no stop is measured in the segment, and no rider message named any place [F3][F8][F9][RD-3].

RD-3(c) then governs the stop/wait line: the waiting charge of $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is RydeTAXI meter waiting time for an in-trip stop and is collected, not refunded [F5][RD-3]. RD-6 fails on the record: route disputes upheld against this driver in the last 90 days are 0 [F18], so no flag_account is warranted [RD-6].

Because the sole off-route segment is exempt, RD-2 yields no refundable distance and the allowed amount is zero: the rate check is $42.36 ÷ 30.04 km = $1.4101/km [F7], and the disputed metreage 5.03 km × $1.4101/km = $7.10 [F3][F4] is not recoverable once the consent excuses the segment [RD-2][RD-5]. The excess-distance line of $7.88 [F4] likewise covers only that unexcused-segment metreage and is not separately refundable. The claimant's assertion that the alternative was "not faster" is a disagreement with route quality, not a clause; the rider's own message authorised the route, and the time gain is not something the record settles (12 min for 5.03 extra km [F3], CEX band 4 [F13] versus AYE band 2 [F12]), so it does not create a refund [RD-5]. The claim therefore fails and the charged fare stands, with the RD-1 breach recorded.
